title: Take-home pay calculator for Canada (2026)
desc: Estimate your 2026 take-home pay after income tax, CPP or QPP and EI in Ontario, Quebec, BC, Alberta, Manitoba and Nova Scotia. Free, in six languages.
lead: Enter your salary or hourly wage to see roughly how much reaches your bank account after tax and payroll deductions in 2026.
avg: About {pct} of your pay goes to tax and contributions.
empty: Enter an amount to see your estimate.
note: Estimate for 2026 using only the basic credits every employee gets. Your real pay can differ by a few percent. The calculation runs in your browser; nothing you type is sent or saved.

items: Your employer takes income tax, pension contributions (CPP, or QPP in Quebec) and Employment Insurance (EI) from every paycheque.
Income tax has two parts, federal and provincial. Both go up in steps as you earn more.
The calculator uses 2026 tax rates and the basic personal amount, which means the first part of your income is not taxed.
In Quebec, you also pay Quebec Parental Insurance Plan premiums, and your federal tax is reduced by 16.5%.
Other tax credits, such as tuition, medical expenses or child care
RRSP or FHSA contributions, union dues and workplace benefits, which change your pay
Benefits you may receive, such as the Canada Child Benefit or the GST/HST credit
Provinces and territories not listed here; use the CRA's official calculator for those
Fill in a TD1 form when you start a job so your employer takes the right amount of tax
File a tax return every spring, even with low income; you may get money back and qualify for benefits
If you started working part way through the year, your employer may have taken more tax than you owe, so you may get a refund
Check your pay stub: it should show gross pay, each deduction and your net pay
